 Hemlo Mining (TSX:HMMC) Stock May Be Overvalued On Current Earnings Expectations
 Sasha Jovanovic Wed, November 4, 2026 at 6:10 PM PST 4 min read HMMC.TO +2.71% 
 Hemlo Mining has seen its stock price move around sharply in recent years, which puts a spotlight on whether today's valuation can be supported by its earnings profile. With the share price now at about C$5.06, investors are asking how much of the recent history is already reflected in what the business currently earns. 
 Over the past 3 years the share price has delivered a very large gain. Any assessment now hinges on whether that kind of move lines up with the company's earnings power. 
 With attention increasingly on how efficiently Hemlo Mining turns its projects into sustainable profits and cash flow, any change in cost control or capital needs can quickly shift how its earnings support the current share price. 
 Your read on Hemlo Mining is one view; the desks covering it have another. See what analysts think Hemlo Mining's shares could be worth . 
 The issue now is whether Hemlo Mining's recent share price level is justified by the earnings the business is generating today. 
 If you are weighing Hemlo Mining against other metals and mining opportunities, it can help to compare it with 34 elite gold producer stocks . 
 Does Hemlo Mining Look Pricey on Earnings? 
 The P/E ratio is a useful starting point for Hemlo Mining because it links what you pay today with the earnings already on the table. At around 66.0x earnings, the stock trades at a much richer multiple than the wider Metals and Mining group, where the average is about 13.4x, and also above the broader peer set on roughly 18.4x. 
 The fair-value model that adjusts for Hemlo Mining's own growth profile, profitability and risk points to a lower P/E than where the shares change hands today, which flags the stock as overvalued on this lens. For you as a shareholder, that gap means a lot of future execution strength is already baked into the price and leaves less room for disappointment to be reflected without pressure on the multiple.
